# Authored Office test fixtures

`word-soft-hyphens/` contains16 MIT-authored Word controls: optional w:softHyphen versus literal U+00AD in w:t, Arial10/Calibri11 in four faces, narrow and wide paper. `reference.json` binds pure source bytes and independent pinned-Word source/edit/save/reopen observations; `baselines.json` binds245 physical exact24 line-box origins across18pages, with every native source glyph unchanged by measurement shading. No Office document content or fonts are distributed. The browser lifecycle, keyboard-insertion and legacy-recovery tests keep native file, encoded-text, glyph, visual and physical-keyboard gates separate; full pagination remains open.

`word-first-save-no-settings/` contains four MIT-authored Latin-1 sources derived by removing the optional settings part and its package registration from `word-pdf-latin1/`. Source bytes and controls are bound in `reference.json`; no third-party content or font binaries are included. Independent source/edit/save/reopen evidence is `.local/word-first-save-no-settings/native-v1`. The permanent first-save and native-return workflows preserve original bytes, settings mode, unrelated parts and editing history; direct PDF glyph and complete pagination parity remain open.

The24 `word-compatibility-*.docx` files and `native-word-compatibility.json` are MIT-authored variants of the existing paragraph-layout fixture. They bind23 native reopens/effective modes/WordPerfect flags/saved DOCX/PDFs and one native rejection. Cases include absent/explicit/future/duplicate settings, renamed and orphan settings parts, and legacy WordPerfect justification. Source originals remain unchanged; no font binaries are included. `.local/word-compatibility/native-v3` contains current evidence; v1/v2 retain failed instrumentation attempts. Native mode coercion is recorded separately from Noffice's conservative unresolved metadata for unknown/conflicting settings. No native UI or complete justification parity is claimed.

`native-word-paragraph-indent-input.json` binds 168 independently saved native body/header physical-indent inputs, including signed half-twip rounding and ±1,584pt boundaries. Producer `.local/probe-paragraph-indent-input.ps1` and promoter `.local/promote-paragraph-indent-input.py` retain input/error/COM/XML/hash evidence under `.local/word-story-paragraph-layout/indent-input-native-v1`. The shared original DOCX is the public MIT-authored paragraph-layout header source. Numeric authoring does not certify extreme-indent rendering or native UI.

`native-word-story-paragraph-layout.json` binds22 independent native header/footer alignment, physical-indent and paragraph-break cases and44 source/edited DOCX files. `.local/probe-story-paragraph-layout.ps1` prepares MIT authored source copies with wrapped Arial10 text; `.local/prepare-story-paragraph-layout.py` validates hashes before promotion. Word-saved originals and PDF/property receipts remain under `.local/word-story-paragraph-layout/native-v1`. No font binaries are distributed; flag metadata in short stories does not certify overflow/native-UI behavior.

`native-word-line-spacing-input.json` binds77 independent installed-Word numeric entry cases and four below-minimum imports. The synthetic `word-line-spacing-tiny-{auto,exact}-*.docx` files modify only the third header paragraph's spacing in the existing project-authored header grid fixture; they contain no user data or font binaries. Native saves preserve these small imported values, while numeric reapplication rejects them. Local source/native hashes and producers are recorded in the active Word contract. Numeric entry evidence does not certify native dialog interaction or tiny-line glyph rendering.

`word-script-scopes/` contains six project-authored Arial10 sources and36 native-formatted DOCX copies. `native-word-script-scopes.json` records independent installed-Word paragraph-mark/inline Sup/Sub formatting, caret/selection, TypeText and Undo/Redo/reopen snapshots. Source, native executable and producer hashes bind local captures in `.local/word-script-scopes/native-v2/`. `native-word-paragraph-replacement.json` adds12 baseline TypeText/Undo/Redo controls with smart paragraph selection off/on; `native-word-script-history.json` adds six end-caret formatting-history/reopened queries. `native-word-script-leaders.json` binds eight native Arial10 script dot-leader geometry profiles and their PDF hashes. `native-word-script-prefix.json` adds six independent prefix Q/history/reopen cases, including Word’s paragraph-terminal navigation bookmark. `native-word-script-provenance.json` binds eight independently authored copied/created-story script controls (corrected native-v2 selection/history). `native-word-script-single-lines.json` and `word-script-single-lines/` bind thirty Arial10 Single script/paragraph-mark controls across body/header/footer; unchanged shaded glyphs independently establish line boundaries. These synthetic fixtures use the project fixture license below and include no font binaries. Object-model evidence does not certify native foreground interaction or full script/pagination parity.

`word-ligatures-*.docx` and `native-word-ligatures.json` contain 24 project-authored Calibri fixtures: all 16 Word ligature combinations plus eight default/paragraph/character/direct inheritance cases. Native run and paragraph-mark properties were captured independently with the pinned installed Word executable. Source/PDF/native-report hashes are retained; full local captures are under `.local/word-ligatures/`. No font binaries are distributed. These fixtures do not certify complete font shaping or UI parity.

`word-tab-leader-story-*.docx` and `native-word-tab-leader-stories.json`: seven independently authored two-page header/footer fixtures, five leader styles,73pt left margin and measured font/color contexts. Installed Word source/header-edited captures supply28 numeric reference pages; local producer/native receipts are bound in the active Word contract. `word-tab-leaders.docx` is a synthetic 95-paragraph leader source. `native-word-tab-leaders.json` records independent native glyph positions, font sizes and colors; the geometry fixture adds 90 cases at three physical margins and positive/negative indents, while `native-word-tab-leader-fonts.json` records finite printer-cell advances. `native-word-tab-leader-baselines.json` binds 95 independently shaded exact40 paragraph baselines with unchanged native glyph matrices. The finite profiles cover Arial10 regular/bold/italic, Arial20 regular, Times New Roman10 and Calibri11. Producer/source/native hashes are retained in the fixtures; private raw evidence is under `.local/word-tab-leaders`, `.local/word-tab-leader-origins` and `.local/word-tab-leader-render`. `native-word-tab-bars.json` records independently shaded line boxes and unchanged native black bar strokes for 18 synthetic paragraphs (19 line boxes), including empty/hard lines, exact/automatic/minimum spacing, negative/multiple stops and font/color/indent cases. The requested nonembedded Inter case paints Corbel in the installed Word; `fontLimit`, `paintedFonts` and `fontReviewHash` preserve that distinction. No Microsoft font binaries are distributed. Geometry acceptance does not certify pixel-identical browser/native bar ink or the full pagination checkbox.

No Microsoft fonts are distributed in these fixtures. `word-tab-legacy-*.noffice` are five actual archived pre-tab-build backups, including saved body/header edits and a fresh header; `native-word-tab-legacy.json` binds their archive/producer/source hashes. `word-line-metrics.docx` is authored for Noffice and distributed under the repository MIT license. It contains six test paragraphs, mixed Arial 10/20pt runs, empty/terminal lines and two sections. No font files or third-party document content are embedded. Its author/last-editor core metadata is set to Noffice.

The baseline was saved by the pinned Word 2016 installation. This separates spacing edits from first-save normalization of a different producer's OOXML. The original generated-source comparison exposed a roughly 0.123pt horizontal glyph shift in an untouched paragraph after native saving; that separate compatibility case remains unresolved. Explicitly enabling OpenType features did not eliminate it, and that experiment was removed.

Recreate deliberately (this replaces the authored fixture; rerun all dependent evidence afterward):

```powershell
node scripts/probe-word-line-metrics.mjs --raw
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/verify-word-line-metrics.ps1 -Create
python scripts/prepare-word-line-metrics-fixture.py
node scripts/probe-word-line-metrics.mjs
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/verify-word-line-metrics.ps1 -SourceOnly
```

The metadata sanitizer preserves XML namespace declarations, including prefixes used inside `xsi:type` values. Native validation is required after regeneration. Current SHA-256: `62c21ac147550c16df809f1f28905abb1705a87e815b19b42d37a5956fe25ad4`.


## Word font cascade fixture

`word-font-cascade.docx` is Noffice-authored MIT test content derived from the spacing fixture and saved by the pinned installed Word build. Core author/editor metadata is replaced with Noffice; no fonts or user documents are embedded. It adds a 14pt paragraph-style ancestry, an 18pt character style, the existing 20pt direct run and distinct 24pt/30pt paragraph marks. It retains a fully empty paragraph and hard breaks. Native Word supplies the independent font expectations.

Regeneration: `node scripts/probe-word-line-metrics.mjs --cascade --raw`, `powershell.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/verify-word-line-metrics.ps1 -Cascade -Create`, then `python scripts/prepare-word-line-metrics-fixture.py --cascade`. Tests consume this checked-in Word-saved baseline via `fontCascadeFixture()`; `rawFontCascadeFixture()` retains the producer variant. The raw variant's first-save page-boundary run splitting exposes a small horizontal PDF difference in untouched wrapped text. This remains a recorded compatibility gap, not a waived pixel tolerance. Browser/native comparisons use the same saved source, and the raw diagnostics remain under `.local/word-font-cascade/raw-producer-evidence`.

`native-powerpoint-coarse-ui.json` records eight independently captured native Position-pane/history/reopen states for slide 1 / leaf 2. Capture using `scripts/verify-powerpoint-coarse-ui.ps1`; current comparisons verify all eight states against this authoring-time oracle without replacing expected values. ## Word mixed-size soft wrapping

`word-glyph-fonts.docx` and `native-word-glyph-fonts.json` add 28 independently authored regular Arial paragraph calibrations: seven sizes from 10 to 40pt in Single, 1.5, Double and 50pt minimum spacing. The DOCX reuses only the existing Noffice-authored MIT package shell, contains numbered probe text and cyan measurement backgrounds, and embeds no user text or fonts. The checked JSON records authoring-time Word/script/source/font/PDF hashes and native baselines; later comparisons bind current scripts separately. Local native-saved copies remain under `.local/word-glyph-fonts`.

Deliberate regeneration only: `python scripts/word-glyph-fonts-fixture.py`, then `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify-word-glyph-fonts.ps1` and `python scripts/inspect-word-glyph-fonts.py --record`. Review changed native rows before replacing acceptance. Ordinary verification omits `--record` and must match the existing checked rows and font hash. The original mixed-wrap oracle below is unchanged; it independently exercises the profile in editing and printed PDFs. [Baseline scope and limits](../../docs/parity/contracts/W-TEXT-UNIFORM-LINES.md#bounded-native-glyph-baseline-continuation).

`word-mixed-wrap.docx` and `native-word-mixed-wrap.json` are Noffice-authored MIT content: two paragraphs of numbered words in Arial 10/20/30pt, with 10/40pt paragraph marks and two sentinels. No user text or fonts are embedded; core author/editor fields are sanitized to Noffice. The checked JSON captures independent native word-line identities and paragraph backgrounds for source, Double, 50pt minimum, Single, size editing and caret typing.

Deliberate regeneration: run `node scripts/word-mixed-wrap-fixture.mjs`, `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify-word-mixed-wrap.ps1 -Create`, then the generator with `--prepare`. Copy `.local/word-mixed-wrap/source.docx` to the checked DOCX. Run the native verifier with `-Reference`, `scripts/probe-word-paragraph-boxes.ps1 -MixedWrap`, then `python scripts/inspect-word-mixed-wrap.py --record`. Review all changed identities/coordinates before replacing acceptance; native-save timestamps change source hashes. Ordinary comparisons use `-Compare`, the probe, the inspector's `--compare` mode and the separate PDF verifier. Local authored measurement copies and fonts stay local. [Scope and exact handoff](../../docs/parity/contracts/W-TEXT-UNIFORM-LINES.md#paragraph-coordinate-and-mixed-wrap-continuation).

### Excel shaped-reference / SUMPRODUCT fixture

`excel-sumproduct.xlsx` and `native-excel-sumproduct.json` are MIT-authored, generated by the installed hash-pinned Excel baseline with `scripts/verify-excel-sumproduct.ps1`. There is no external/private workbook content. The closed source package's author/company fields are sanitized before the reference hash and saved-file reopening check. The 48 formulas span dimensions, constants, singleton expansion, coercion/errors, names, tables and legacy scalar-function interactions. Five independent stages edit/delete/error A2, enter a formula in Calls!D8, and change Items' quantity H3. Native comparison also re-edits B2 in independently authored and browser-exported copies and saves/reopens each.

Deliberate regeneration only: `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify-excel-sumproduct.ps1` creates the authored local workbook/reference and copies both checked fixtures. Ordinary validation: build, run `npx.cmd playwright test tests/excel-sumproduct.spec.ts --workers=1`, then `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/verify-excel-sumproduct.ps1 -Compare` and `python scripts/compare-excel-sumproduct.py`. The latter checks all actual XLSX caches before considering native recalculation, plus exact 144-DPI PDFs for exports and native re-edits. `--negative-control` perturbs one cached value in memory, must exit 1, and leaves canonical artifacts intact. Native automation uses an idle owned instance with macros/link refresh disabled and preferences restored; private fixtures remain local. Full function/array/UI/locale parity is not claimed.


### Active Word pagination fixtures

The six `word-implicit-final-{1,2,3}-sections-{omitted,empty}.docx` files are MIT-authored synthetic section/story fixtures. `native-word-implicit-final-sections.json` binds the originals, pinned Word captures and five independent materialization comparisons. An omitted final section uses the captured de-DE Normal-template A4 defaults; an explicitly empty final element uses Letter. The reference records the template hash, not its contents; no template or font binary is distributed. Native originals, actual edited files and PDF evidence remain under `.local/word-implicit-final-sections/`. COM boundary deletion and default Smart Cut and Paste must be distinguished from actual keyboard behavior; the complete interaction matrix remains required.

The six `word-implicit-final-return-*.docx` files and `native-word-implicit-final-returns.json` continue those synthetic documents through actual browser export, native Word editing, save and reopen. Only core creator/editor metadata is sanitized. Each sanitized source preserves the native page render exactly; no embedded fonts are included. The subsequent browser editing/history/reload tests retain unrelated parts and verify the new typing-session registration separately. Word's unsaved and saved/reopened rendering states are compared separately in `.local/word-implicit-final-sections/returns-native-v1/`; an exact saved-file comparison does not certify the unsaved state or native keyboard interaction.

`word-variable-{mixed,single,keep}.docx` plus `native-word-variable-pagination.json` cover nonempty mixed hard lines, variable page flow and keep/widow/break-before edits. Ten `word-section-flow-*.docx` files plus `native-word-section-flow.json` cover six continuous/equal-column layouts, two keep/widow interactions and two still-guarded unequal/nextColumn cases. Five `word-keep-overflow-*.docx` files plus `native-word-keep-overflow.json` independently capture oversized kept paragraphs and preceding-text interactions. Native actual edited exports and PDFs are verified by the maintained variable/section-flow scripts; see the [current handoff](../../docs/parity/contracts/W-TEXT-UNIFORM-LINES.md#current-handoff-after-column-keep-verification).

Twenty-four `word-inline-flow-*.docx` files and `native-word-inline-flow.json` independently cover eight page/column-break shapes under exact, automatic and minimum spacing, including terminal insertion lines. Eight `word-forced-keep-*.docx` files and `native-word-forced-keep.json` expose keep/widow/manual-break combinations; six initial allocator mismatches are fixed and passed browser/native comparison at the recorded checkpoint. Twenty-eight `word-ui-flow-*.docx` files / `native-word-ui-flow.json` capture actual native keyboard paragraph splitting, history, cursor offsets and typing under those spacing rules and four start/selected-range contexts. Independent paragraph-background captures establish comparable coordinates without moving any glyph. Native discovery temporarily disables sentence capitalization and restores the original preference; broader/default proofing behavior remains required. The earlier eight-case acceptance is historical while expanded browser/native/glyph gates are refreshed.

`word-exact-baselines.docx` / `native-word-exact-baselines.json` contain twelve regular Arial size/line-height combinations, including clipped oversized glyphs. Independent native PDF paragraph backgrounds establish exact baselines within the existing 0.15pt bound, with all glyph matrices unchanged by shading. These references do not certify the unimplemented clipped-glyph renderer or other fonts. The maintained flow glyph comparer checks actual source/edited print origins, colors and physical font sizes separately from native exported-file pixel equality.
